LESSON: WRITING 10.4.1 CREATIVE WRITING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.4: Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What words do we use to describe objects, people or events?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. use appropriate adjectives to describe a person, object or a place
2. create a descriptive composition on a variety of topics

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 10.4.1 CREATIVE WRITING
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 10.4.1 CREATIVE WRITING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Use appropriate adjectives to describe a person, object or a place

What this means
In this part you learn to use appropriate adjectives to describe a person, object or a place. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use appropriate adjectives to describe a person, object or a place.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use appropriate adjectives to describe a person, object or a place. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Create a descriptive composition on a variety of topics

What this means
In this part you learn to create a descriptive composition on a variety of topics. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: create a descriptive composition on a variety of topics.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can create a descriptive composition on a variety of topics. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: use appropriate adjectives to describe a person, object or a place)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing to a partner. (skill: create a descriptive composition on a variety of topics)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: use appropriate adjectives to describe a person, object or a place.
3. Practise this skill: create a descriptive composition on a variety of topics.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What words do we use to describe objects, people or events?
2. How can we make our descriptions more interesting?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: use appropriate adjectives to describe a person, object or a place.
5. Be able to: create a descriptive composition on a variety of topics.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
